description: Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, is a classic Indian dish celebrated for its rich, creamy tomato-based gravy and tender pieces of marinated chicken. This iconic curry offers a perfect balance of smoky tanginess and subtle sweetness, making it a favorite across the globe. It is best enjoyed with naan bread or fragrant basmati rice, creating a truly comforting and indulgent meal.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces, yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice. Mix well to ensure the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally for 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter and 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until the chicken is browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes on each side. Remove the chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another tablespoon of butter. Add chopped onions and saute until translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in the remaining ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Cook for 30 seconds.

instructions.title: Simmer and Blend the Gravy
instructions.text: Add the tomato puree, soaked cashews, red chili powder, turmeric powder, and salt to the pan. Bring to a simmer and cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes soften and the oil starts to separate. Remove from heat, discard the bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and cardamom pods. Let it cool slightly, then transfer to a blender and blend until completely smooth. Strain the gravy through a fine-mesh sieve for an extra smooth texture, if desired.

instructions.title: Finish the Butter Chicken
instructions.text: Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium heat. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter, sugar, and crushed kasuri methi. Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. If the gravy is too thick, add a splash of water to reach your desired consistency.

instructions.title: Combine and Serve
instructions.text: Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir gently to coat the chicken thoroughly. Cook for another 2-3 minutes to heat the chicken through. Finally, stir in the heavy cream. Do not boil after adding cream. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve hot with naan, roti, or basmati rice.

tips: For truly tender chicken, marinate it overnight if possible, allowing the flavors to deeply penetrate the meat.
For a richer and creamier gravy, ensure your cashews are well soaked and blended until absolutely smooth, or add a tablespoon of almond meal.
Garnish with a swirl of fresh cream and chopped cilantro just before serving for an enhanced aroma and visual appeal.
article:
Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani as it's traditionally known, holds a revered spot in the pantheon of Indian cuisine. This globally adored dish is a symphony of creamy, tangy, and mildly spiced flavors, making it a perfect Indian lunch recipe that satisfies the soul and the palate. Its rich, velvety texture and tender chicken pieces swim in a luscious tomato-based gravy, making it an irresistible choice for any meal, particularly a hearty midday feast. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality experience in your own kitchen, you're in the right place. We're about to embark on a culinary journey to master the art of making the ultimate Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

At its heart, Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a classic Indian curry born in the bustling kitchens of Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi in the 1950s. The story goes that leftover tandoori chicken pieces were simmered in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream, creating a dish so revolutionary it quickly captured the hearts of millions. "Murgh" translates to chicken, and "Makhani" means buttery, perfectly describing the dish's signature characteristic. It's a mild curry, eschewing the fiery heat often associated with Indian food for a more nuanced flavor profile. The magic lies in the balance: the sweetness of tomatoes and a touch of sugar, the richness of butter and cream, and the aromatic depth of kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) and garam masala. This combination creates a comforting, luxurious gravy that coats every piece of succulent chicken, making Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani not just a meal, but an experience. It’s a dish that transcends cultural boundaries, becoming a staple in Indian restaurants worldwide and a beloved comfort food for many.

## Ingredients You Need

To create this iconic Indian lunch recipe, you'll need a selection of fresh and aromatic ingredients.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken (thighs or breast), cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   Salt to taste

For the Makhani Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes or 3-4 large fresh tomatoes, pureed
*   1/2 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, optional but recommended for smoothness)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon ground coriander
*   1/2 teaspoon ground cumin
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/4 teaspoon cardamom powder (or 2-3 green cardamom pods)
*   1 bay leaf
*   1 tablespoon sugar (or to taste, balances tomato acidity)
*   1 teaspoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   Salt to taste
*   Water or chicken broth, as needed

For Garnish:
*   Fresh coriander leaves, chopped
*   A swirl of heavy cream

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani might seem elaborate, but breaking it down makes it entirely manageable for a delicious Indian lunch.

1.  Marinate the Chicken: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor and tenderness.

2.  Cook the Chicken: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer (cook in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding). Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.

3.  Prepare the Gravy Base: In the same pan, add the butter. Once melted, add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and bay leaf, cooking for another minute until fragrant.

4.  Build the Gravy Flavor: Stir in the turmeric powder, red chili powder, ground coriander, ground cumin, garam masala, and cardamom powder (if using ground, otherwise add pods with onions). Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, until fragrant.

5.  Add Tomatoes and Cashews: Pour in the crushed or pureed tomatoes. If using soaked cashews, drain them and add them to the pan now. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the oil starts to separate.

6.  Blend the Gravy: Remove the bay leaf. Carefully transfer the mixture to a blender (or use an immersion blender). Blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky texture, pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.

7.  Finish the Gravy: Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the sugar, kasuri methi (crush it between your palms to release its aroma), and salt to taste. Stir well.

8.  Combine and Simmer: Add the cooked chicken pieces to the gravy. Pour in the heavy cream and stir gently to combine. If the gravy is too thick, add a little water or chicken broth to reach your desired consistency. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the rich sauce.

9.  Serve: Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and a final swirl of cream.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that authentic, mouth-watering Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani at home is all about a few key techniques and ingredient choices.

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt tenderizes the chicken, and the spices infuse deep flavor. Longer is always better for succulent results.
*   **Chicken Thighs vs. Breast:** While breast meat works, boneless, skinless chicken thighs are generally preferred for Butter Chicken as they remain more tender and moist during cooking.
*   **Smooth Gravy is a Must:** For that signature creamy texture, blend your gravy base until absolutely smooth. Straining it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending is an extra step that makes a noticeable difference.
*   **The Power of Kasuri Methi:** This dried fenugreek leaf is non-negotiable for authentic Butter Chicken flavor. Toast it lightly in a dry pan for 30 seconds before crushing and adding to the gravy to maximize its aromatic impact.
*   **Balance of Sweet and Tangy:** Tomatoes can be quite acidic. A touch of sugar (or even honey) helps balance this acidity and enhances the overall sweetness, creating a harmonious flavor profile for your Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani.
*   **Quality Ingredients:** Use good quality butter and fresh cream. These are prominent flavors, so their quality will shine through.
*   **Let it Rest:** Like many stews and curries, Butter Chicken often tastes even better the next day, as the flavors have more time to meld and deepen.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a versatile dish that pairs beautifully with a variety of accompaniments. For a classic Indian lunch experience, serve it hot with freshly baked naan bread, roti, or paratha, perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich gravy. It's equally delicious alongside fluffy basmati rice, plain or fragrant jeera rice. To complete the meal, consider adding a simple side salad of sliced cucumber, onion, and tomatoes, or a cooling raita (yogurt dip) to cut through the richness. A sprinkle of fresh coriander and a final dollop or swirl of cream just before serving adds both visual appeal and an extra touch of luxury.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a masterpiece, you can certainly adapt it to suit dietary preferences or ingredient availability.

*   **Vegetarian Option:** Easily transform this into Paneer Makhani by replacing the chicken with cubed paneer (Indian cottage cheese), which can be lightly fried before adding to the gravy. Tofu or mixed vegetables also work wonderfully.
*   **Healthier Twist:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or substitute some of the cream with Greek yogurt (stirred in at the very end to prevent curdling) for a lighter version.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the red chili powder to your preference. For more heat, add green chilies along with the ginger-garlic paste. For less, reduce or omit the chili powder entirely.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have a nut allergy, you can omit the cashews. The gravy might be slightly less thick, but still delicious. You can add a tablespoon of poppy seeds (soaked and blended) or a tiny bit of cornstarch slurry at the end for thickness if desired.
*   **Dairy-Free:** Substitute butter with a plant-based alternative and heavy cream with full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream for a dairy-free rendition.

Whether you stick to the traditional recipe or experiment with these variations, the essence of Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani – its comforting richness and aromatic depth – remains.

Making Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani at home is a truly rewarding experience. It's a dish that embodies the warmth and hospitality of Indian cuisine, offering a burst of flavor and comfort with every spoonful. Perfect for a leisurely weekend lunch or a special weeknight treat, this iconic Indian lunch recipe is sure to become a cherished addition to your culinary repertoire. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to delight your taste buds with one of the world's most beloved curries.
